_comment: Team template (team config, schema 1) → product/<team>/team.json. Step T0: draft it with python3 scripts/new_team.py --init <team> --field "..." --members "Name One;Name Two;Name Three", complete it by hand following these notes, then run python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json, which scaffolds the team from it and the templates in this folder; every later workflow and script (team_status.py, the scripts/workflows/*.js runs) reads it.

All values below are fictional placeholders (the same fictional team, product/example-team, that scripts/workflows/examples/ uses for dry runs; its first two members are the dry-run members). Real team.json files carry no _comment key. See product/dfo-team for a worked example (team.json).
schema: always 1. team: folder name under product/ (lowercase, hyphenated). title: display name used in the README, the roundtable and the triggers.
field: the field and the tradition within it that the team covers; name the neighbouring traditions that are not represented.
language: language of the member skills and their paper cards (cards for a researcher who writes in English are written in English).
created: ISO date of T0. roundtable: slug of the roundtable skill folder inside the team folder.
chase_hints (team level): field-wide legitimate open-access repositories that team-chase.js searches first (preprint servers, open proceedings, report series).
members: 3-6 researchers chosen for complementary lenses and documented disagreements. Per member:

slug: skill folder name (lowercase, hyphenated full name). name: display name. surname: used for lens labels (@Surname, [Surname lens], add/drop Surname), so it must be unique within the team: when two members share a surname, write e.g. "N. Higham" and "D. Higham".
living: false marks a historical lens (its skill reflects work up to the researcher's death).
hint: one line that disambiguates the researcher in searches (institutions, years, signature work).

scholar: Google Scholar user id (the user= value in the profile URL), or empty if there is none: the harvest then searches Scholar by name once and otherwise builds the list from DBLP and the homepage (find the DBLP pid with python3 scripts/dblp_works.py --name "<name>"). dblp: DBLP pid if known. orcid, homepage: empty if unknown.
chase_hints: member-specific open sources (institutional report series, homepage paper pages), with any access quirks (e.g. a host that only works over http).
student_mode: true gives the skill a Student Mode plus references/proof-playbook.md, open-problems.md and reading-path.md.
